headline: High: ms-swift can write and execute code while PaddleOCR processes documents, creating default-path data leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt injection is lower because no shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, ms-swift can read/write files and run shell/Python, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images; if the operator bridges them via files or copy-paste, malicious document text could influence downstream prompts. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF the operator passes PaddleOCR output into ms-swift prompts or files without sanitization, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge, attacker-controlled document text can propagate.
mitigations: Use a one-way export format that strips instructions before ms-swift reads OCR output.
Add a short prompt-sanitization step before any handoff.
Keep the agents in separate directories.
Review OCR text for embedded commands before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches secrets and many file-backed artifacts, and PaddleOCR processes documents and images. With no stated isolation or shared-workspace controls, a default file handoff can expose sensitive document contents to ms-swift or leak ms-swift logs/checkpoints into OCR workflows. The interaction is inferred from profiles, so uncertainty remains.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace directory, document contents can flow between them.
IF ms-swift logs or training outputs are readable by PaddleOCR, sensitive text may be exposed.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent.
Restrict file permissions on logs and outputs.
Avoid placing secrets in shared OCR inputs.
Delete intermediate OCR artifacts after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift can execute shell, install packages, read/write files, and spawn subprocesses; PaddleOCR can run browsers and use APIs. Even without explicit shared writes, overlapping filesystem and network-adjacent activity can conflict if they operate on the same resources. The profiles do not state locking or isolation, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or inconsistent state can occur.
IF both agents target the same external API or browser session, resource contention can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories.
Run only one writer per shared resource.
Close browser sessions before ms-swift jobs.
Use per-agent API credentials.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR turns documents into structured text, and ms-swift can consume files and run Python/shell, so A's output can become B's input or vice versa without a documented verification step. That creates a realistic cascade where OCR or generated text is treated as authoritative. No evidence shows automatic action-taking, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into ms-swift prompts or scripts without validation, errors can propagate.
IF ms-swift-generated text is rendered or acted on by PaddleOCR workflows, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Add a human review step between agents.
Validate OCR confidence before reuse.
Reject outputs that lack source citations.
Keep action-taking systems separate from OCR text generation.
requires-engineering: implement schema validation on handoff data.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only docs-only verified, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. ms-swift handles hub/sdk tokens and PaddleOCR handles documents/images, but the pairwise compliance breach is not evidenced. Because the rubric requires documented gaps for higher severity, low is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF the deployment routes EU personal data through a non-EU-only environment, compliance risk increases.
IF retention policies differ between the two tools in the operator's deployment, a mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Confirm data residency before processing regulated data.
Avoid sending secrets through OCR inputs.
Document retention for logs and outputs.
Use separate environments for regulated and unregulated data.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
